name: Reconstructed Canal Street blacksmith shop

documented_range.note: An invented count-unit for July 1835, not evidence that this particular building existed.

change_note: T-1766 adds this reconstructed trade roof without moving an existing building.

placement.position_note: The street exists in the cadastral evidence; this roof does not. Its front is set one metre outside the drawn east corridor edge. The layout follows the West memo and current trade placement policy, with open gaps and rear work ground; the station is invented and claims no recovered lot or address.
placement.symbolic_location: Reconstructed east frontage of Canal Street between Lake and Randolph

what_it_supplies: A 665-roof production target with independently reconcilable group, district, level, and construction totals.
Thirty-five architectural family definitions with dimensional and massing bands.
District character, spacing, variation, finish, and chronology constraints for a July 1835 reconstruction.
A required distinction between named documentary landmarks and anonymous inferred infill.
what_it_does_not_supply: A surviving July 1835 building census or parcel-by-parcel roof register.
Exact locations, dimensions, appearance, occupants, or construction dates for anonymous roofs.
Authority to replace stronger building-specific evidence already represented in the dataset.

research_note: RECONSTRUCTED, NOT A RECOVERED ADDRESS. The West memo bounds mixed trade on the Canal approach; the live programme leaves room for two stores and two workshops. C3 and C4 use remaining store-family capacity because C1 and C2 are already full. Exact existence, location, dimensions, finish and form remain inventions. Any reconstructed occupants are separately graded by their own records.
